title: Maximum and Minimum Sums of at Most Size K Subsequences
summary: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, calculate the sum of the maximum and minimum elements of all subsequences of the array with at most k elements, then return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, calculate the sum of the maximum and minimum elements of all subsequences of the array with at most k elements, then return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Consider every nonempty index subsequence containing at most k elements, with k <= min(70,len(nums)).
Sum the minimum and maximum of every such subsequence modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: After sorting, a value is an extreme according to how many elements are chosen on one side of it.
Accumulate binomial counts for choosing zero through k-1 companion indices.
At each size add value*C(index,size) as a maximum and value*C(n-1-index,size) as a minimum, updating combinations in place.
Every subsequence is counted once by its chosen minimum and once by its chosen maximum; sorting affects values, not index-choice multiplicity.
editorial: Every subsequence is counted once by its chosen minimum and once by its chosen maximum; sorting affects values, not index-choice multiplicity.

tests.explanation: Three singleton contributions total twelve, and the three length-two contributions total twelve, giving twenty-four.
Each singleton contributes its value twice, so the result is twenty-two.
